Surah al-Tur (The Mount)

﴿By the Mount (al-Tur)﴾ Al-Tur in Syriac means "the mountain," and what is meant here is Tur Sinin (Mount Sinai), a mountain in Madyan where Musa (peace be upon him) heard the speech of Allah the Exalted.

﴿And a Book inscribed﴾ — written in an orderly manner, for "saṭr" (line) is the arrangement of the letters that are written. What is meant by it is: the Qur'an, or the tablets of Moses (peace be upon him), and this is the most fitting with "al-Ṭūr" (the Mount); or what is inscribed in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ); or what the noble recording angels (al-ḥafaẓah) write.

"In a scroll unrolled." Ar-raqq: the skin on which one writes; it is used metaphorically for the sheet on which the Book is written. Their being indefinite is either for magnification, or to indicate that they are not among what people are accustomed to.

﴿And the House that is frequented﴾. That is: the Ka'bah, and its being populated by the pilgrims, the visitors, and those who dwell near it; or it is al-Diraah (the heavenly House), which is in the fourth heaven, and its being populated is the abundance of those who frequent it from among the angels.
"And the raised canopy" (al-saqf al-marfu'). That is, the sky. The fitting placement of this description is not hidden.

﴿And the sea that is filled (al-masjur)﴾. That is: the filled, and it is the encompassing sea, or the kindled, from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze (sujjirat)﴾. So what is meant by it is the genus (al-jins). It is related that God, exalted is He, will make the seas on the Day of Resurrection into fire, with which He will kindle the fire of Hell.
Verse: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾ — that is, it will certainly descend, inevitably. It is the response to the oath.

The Almighty's words, ﴿There is none that can avert it﴾, are either a second predicate of "inna" (indeed), or an attribute of "waqi'" (will fall). And "min dafi'" (from any repeller) is either the subject of the adverbial phrase, or is in the nominative by way of being the agent of it. The "min" is extra, for emphasis.

The singling out of these things for oath-swearing is because they are great matters which point to the greatness of God the Exalted's power, the perfection of His knowledge and wisdom, which indicate His encompassing knowledge of the details of the deeds of His servants and their recording, and which testify to the truthfulness of His reports, of which the sentence sworn to is one.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 9:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when the sky will be convulsed, a convulsion﴾, is a time-clause (zarf) modifying "wāqi'" (will befall), explaining the manner in which it befalls and indicating the utmost of its terror and awfulness. Al-mawr (convulsion): agitation and back-and-forth motion in coming and going. It is also said: it is a movement in the manner of waves. It is said: the sky will revolve as a millstone revolves, and will tilt with its inhabitants like a ship tilting. It is also said: its parts will be disjointed (takhtalifu ajza'uha).

And the mountains will be set in motion, a motion (﴿وَتَسِيرُ الجِبالُ سَيْرًا﴾): that is, they will pass away from the face of the earth and become scattered dust (habaʼ). The emphasis of the two verbs by their verbal nouns (maṣdar, i.e., the verbal noun that reinforces the verb) serves to signal the strangeness of both and their going beyond the familiar limits; that is, a wondrous passing and a marvellous motion whose true nature cannot be comprehended.
Verse 11 of Surah al-Tur (52): ﴿So woe on that Day to the deniers﴾. That is: if that occurs, or if the matter is as it has been mentioned, then woe on the Day when that befalls them.

Those who are in plunging ("khawd") into vain talk, i.e., a strange rushing forward into falsehoods and lies.

Playing: they are amusing themselves, diverting themselves.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 13:

﴿On the Day they will be thrust into the fire of Hell with a violent thrusting.﴾ That is: they will be pushed toward it with a forceful, severe push, with their hands chained to their necks and their forelocks gathered to their feet, and so they will be pushed into the Fire. It is also read as "yud'awna" (from al-du'a', "to be called/summoned"), in which case "da'an" is a circumstantial accusative (hal) meaning "being driven/called forcibly." And "yawma" is either a substitute (badal) for "yawma tamur" (the Day the sky will be in turmoil), or an adverbial object (zarf) governed by a verb understood before His words, Exalted is He:
ﷻ"This is the Fire which you used to deny." That is, it will be said to them so. The meaning of denying it is their denial of the revelation that speaks of it.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is this magic?﴾ is a rebuke and reproach to them, since they used to call it magic, as if it were said: "You used to say of the Qur'an, which speaks this, that it is magic, so this too is magic." The placing of the predicate first is because it is the focal point of the denial and the axis of the rebuke.

﴿Or do you not see?﴾ That is: Or are you blind to what it reports, just as you were blind to the report? Or your sights have been covered, as they were covered in the world according to your claim, when you used to say: ﴿Our eyes have only been intoxicated; rather, we are a people bewitched.﴾

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 16:

﴿Enter it and endure its burning, or do not endure it; it is all the same for you.﴾ That is: enter it and experience its severities; so do whatever you wish of patience and its absence.

﴿It is all the same for you﴾ That is: the two matters are equal in that neither benefits, neither by averting the punishment nor by lessening it. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾ is an explanation for the equality, for since the recompense is necessarily to occur, certainly (p-148) patience and its absence are equal in bringing no benefit.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 17:

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens and bliss.﴾ That is: in what gardens, and what bliss! This is so if the nunation (tanwin) is for magnification (tafkhim, emphasis on greatness); or it means "in gardens" and "bliss" specific to the God-fearing, if the nunation is for variety (tanwi', indicating kinds).

﴿فاكِهِينَ﴾ "Joyful": pleased, delighting, enjoying pleasures.

﴿بِما آتاهم رَبُّهُمْ﴾ "For what their Lord had given them." It is also read as "فَكِهِينَ" and "فاكِهُونَ". The latter is the predicate (*khabar*), and the prepositional phrase (*zarf*) is *laghw* (a complement that is not grammatically essential) attached to the predicate, or it is another predicate.

﴿وَوَقاهم رَبُّهم عَذابَ الجحيم﴾ "And their Lord protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire." It is conjoined (*'atf*) to "آتاهُمْ", with "ما" being a verbal-noun particle (*masdariyyah*), or it is conjoined to the predicate of "إنَّ" (*inna*), or it is a circumstantial clause (*hal*) with "قد" implied. The circumstantial clause may relate either to the hidden pronoun in the predicate or in the circumstantial clause itself, or to the subject of "أتى" or its object, or to both. Mentioning "the Lord" explicitly in place of a pronoun, and attaching it to their pronoun, is for honour and to give the reason.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 19:

﴿Eat and drink﴾, i.e., it will be said to them: eat and drink, eating and drinking.

﴿Wholesome﴾, or the food and drink are wholesome (hanīʾan), that is, free from any disturbance (tanghīs).

﴿For what you used to do﴾: by reason of it (bi-sababihi), or in return for it (bi-muqābalatihi). It has also been said that the bāʾ (bi) is superfluous and that "mā" (ma) is the subject of "hanīʾan," meaning: may what you used to do bring you wholesome enjoyment, i.e., its recompense.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 20:

﴿Reclining on couches arranged in rows﴾ — meaning, lined up.

﴿And We shall pair them with houris, wide-eyed (ḥūr ʿīn)﴾. It has also been read as "biḥūri ʿīnin" (with the genitive construction of the qualified noun to its qualifier), according to the well-known interpretation, and it has been read as "biʿaynin ʿīnin." The preposition bāʾ (bi-) is used even though tazwīj (marrying/pairing) is among the verbs that take two objects directly, because of the meaning of joining and attaching it contains; or it indicates causation (sababiyya), since the meaning is: We made them spouses (azwāj) by means of them, for the state of being spouses is not realized without their being joined to them.

And His saying, ﴿Those who believed﴾ ... etc., is a resumptive sentence (kalam mustaʾnaf), brought to explain the condition of a group of the people of Paradise after explaining the condition of all of them. They are those whose offspring joined them in faith. It is a subject (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is "We shall join them." His saying, ﴿and their offspring followed them﴾, is conjoined (ʿatf) to "believed." It was said to be a parenthetical clause (iʿtiraḍ). His saying, ﴿with faith﴾, is dependent (mutaʿallaq) on "following," meaning: their offspring followed them with a faith that, in general terms, falls short of the rank of the fathers' faith. The inclusion of this qualifier serves to indicate that the ruling applies to complete faith, originally and not by way of attachment.

It was also read as "dhurriyyatuhum" (their offspring, in the plural form) for emphasis on abundance, and "dhirriyyatuhum" with a kasra on the dhal. It was read as "wa-atbaʿnāhum dhurriyyātihim," meaning: We made them followers of them in faith. It was also read as "atbaʿtuhum."

﴿We shall join with them their offspring﴾, that is, in rank, as it is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, exalted is He, raises the offspring of the believer to his rank, even if they are below him, so that his eye may be comforted by them," and then he recited this verse.

﴿And We did not deprive them﴾: and We did not diminish the fathers by this joining.

﴿of their deeds﴾: of the reward of their deeds.

﴿of anything﴾: by giving some of their rewards to their children, so that their reward would be diminished and their rank lowered. Rather, We raised them to their station purely by favor and kindness. It was also read as "alatnāhum," with a kasra on the lam, from "alita, yaʾlatu," like "ʿalima, yaʿlamu." The first is like "ḍaraba, yaḍribu." "Litnāhum" is from "lāta, yalītu," "ātalnāhum" is from "ātala, yu'tilu," and "waltnāhum" is from "walita, yalitu." All of these have one meaning.

Furthermore, it has been said that the relative clause (al-mawṣūl) is conjoined to "ḥūr" (the dark-eyed companions), and the meaning is: We paired them with the ḥūr and with those who believed, that is, with their companions and comrades from among them. Thus they enjoy, at one time, the company of the ḥūr, and at another time, the fellowship of their believing brothers. His saying, ﴿and their offspring followed them﴾, is conjoined to "We paired them." His saying, ﴿with faith﴾, is dependent on what follows it, meaning: by means of a great faith of exalted station, namely the faith of the fathers, We join their offspring to their ranks, even though they do not merit them, as a favor upon them and upon their fathers, so that their joy may be complete and their bliss perfected. Or it means: by means of the faith of a lower station, namely the faith of the offspring, as if it were said: with a degree of faith that does not qualify them for the rank of the fathers, We join them to them.

﴿Every person is in pledge for what he has earned﴾. It was said: "rahīn" is an intensive form (faʿīl) in the sense of a passive participle (maf'ūl), and the meaning is: every person is held as a pledge with Allah, exalted is He, by his righteous deed; if he performs it, he redeems himself, and otherwise it destroys him. It was also said: it is in the sense of an active participle (fāʿil), and the meaning is: every person, by what he has earned, is "rāhin," that is, lasting and firm. This is more fitting to the context, for permanence requires that there be no separation between a person and his deed, and it follows from this that nothing of the fathers' reward be diminished. Thus the sentence serves as a justification (taʿlīl) for what precedes it.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 22:

﴿And We will provide them with fruit and meat of whatever they desire.﴾ And We will increase them, from time to time, in what they had of the beginnings of luxury, with whatever they desire of the various kinds of blessings and the diverse sorts of bounties.

They pass around to one another therein, they and their companions, with utmost desire and longing, as the expression "tanazu'" (passing the cup back and forth, contending for it) indicates.

A cup (kas): that is, wine, named by the name of its container.

No idle talk therein: that is, in its drinking, where they do not speak during the drinking with vain talk and worthless speech.

Nor any sinning: nor do they do anything for which its doer would be charged with sin, were he to do it in the abode of obligation, as is the habit of the drinking companions in this world. Rather, they speak with wise sayings and fine speech, and they do what noble people do. It is also recited as "lā laghwa fīhā wa lā ta'thīma" (with a fatha on both nouns).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 24:

﴿And there will go round among them﴾, i.e., with the cup, ﴿young boys belonging to them﴾, i.e., servants specially assigned to them. It is also said that they are their children who preceded them [in death].

﴿As if they were pearls well-guarded﴾, protected within the shell because of their whiteness and purity; or "stored away" (makhzun), since only what is precious and of high value is stored away. It was said to Qatadah: "This is the servant; so what of the one served?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, the superiority of the one served over the servant is like the superiority of the full moon over the rest of the stars."

And from him (ﷺ), upon whom be prayers and peace: "Indeed, the lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is one who calls his servant from among his servants, and a thousand answer at his door: 'Here I am, here I am!'"

Translation of the passage:

﴿And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another﴾. That is: each of them asks the others about their conditions and their deeds, so that each one is both questioner and questioned; it does not mean that one specific person among them asks another specific person.

(p-150) ﴿They said﴾: that is, those who are questioned, each one of them in reality.

﴿Indeed, we were before﴾: that is, in the world.

﴿among our families, fearful﴾: tender-hearted, fearful of disobeying God Most High, attentive to His obedience, or apprehensive of the outcome.

"So Allah has bestowed favour upon us" — by mercy, or by granting us success in (following) the truth.

"And has protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind" — the punishment of the Fire which penetrates through the pores as the scorching wind (samum) penetrates. It is also read "wa-waqqana" with the doubled letter (shaddah).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 28:

﴿Indeed, we used to call upon Him before.﴾ That is: we used to worship Him, or ask Him for protection (wiqaya).

﴿Indeed, He is the Good (al-Barr)﴾ — the Benevolent.

﴿the Merciful (al-Rahim)﴾ — the one of abundant mercy, who, when He is worshipped, rewards, and when He is asked, responds. It has also been read as "innahu" with a fatha (anna-hu), meaning "because He" (li-annahu).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 29:

﴿So remind, for by the favour of your Lord you are neither a soothsayer nor a madman﴾

Then hold firm to what you are upon of reminding with what has been revealed to you of the verses and the Wise Reminder (al-dhikr al-hakim), and do not concern yourself with what they say of the falsehoods in which there is no good.

﴿You are not, by the favour of your Lord﴾ — by His praise and His bounty — through the truthfulness of prophethood and soundness of intellect.

﴿a soothsayer (kahin) nor a madman (majnun)﴾ as they say. May God fight them; how are they turned away (anna yu'fakun)?

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 30:

﴿Or do they say, "A poet; we await for him the misfortunes of time"?﴾ That is, what unsettles souls and causes them to be startled by the calamities of the age. It has also been said: al-Manun (the misfortunes of time) means death. Originally it is on the pattern fa'ul, from mannahu (he cut it off), because death is a cutting off (qutu'), i.e., "Rather, do they say we await for him the calamities of the age?"

Verse: "Say: Wait, for I am with you among those who wait."

I wait for your destruction, just as you wait for my destruction. And in it is a generous promise of their destruction.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 32:

﴿Or do their minds (ahlamuhum) command them to this?﴾ That is: their intellects ('uquluhum).

﴿To this﴾ That is: to this contradiction in speech, for the soothsayer (kahin) is one of acuteness and precision of insight into matters, while the madman whose intellect is covered has a disordered thought, and the poet is one of measured, coherent, imaginative speech. So how can the attributes of these people come together in one person? The attribution of commanding to the minds (ahlam) is a metaphor for their conveying (the matter) to it.

﴿Or are they a people who are transgressors?﴾ Those who exceed the limits in obstinacy and stubborn opposition, who do not circle around guidance and rectitude. For this reason they say what they say of falsehoods outside the sphere of intellects and reasonable opinions. It has also been read as "bal hum" (rather, they).

Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Rather, they do not believe. (Abu al-Su'ud says:) "Or do they say he has fabricated it," that is: he invented it from his own self.

"Rather, they do not believe." Because of their disbelief and obstinacy, they hurl these falsehoods whose untruth is not hidden from anyone. How could it not be? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is but one of the Arabs, so how could he have produced what all the nations, both Arab and non-Arab, were unable to produce?

(p-151) ﴿So let them produce a statement like it﴾ — like the Qur'an in the qualities by which it stands alone, both in its composition (nazm) and in its meaning.

﴿If they are truthful﴾ in what they claim. Their truthfulness in this would require their ability to produce the like of it, given that they share with him, upon him be blessings and peace, humanity and the Arabic language, together with their long practice of oratory and poetry, their constant engagement with the methods of verse and prose, and their great care in preserving events and days. There is no doubt that the capacity to do something is among the necessary conditions for doing it, and among the motives for being commanded to do so.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 35:

﴿Or were they created from nothing?﴾ That is: or did they come into being and determine this wondrous determination without any originator and determiner? It has also been said: "Or were they created for nothing," i.e. without any purpose of worship and recompense.

﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ Of themselves; therefore they do not worship God, glorified is He.

Or were they created from nothing? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they have no certainty.

That is: when they are asked, "Who created you and created the heavens and the earth?", they say, "God." But they are not certain of what they say; otherwise they would not turn away from His worship.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 37:

﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ That is: the treasuries of His provision and His mercy, so that they could bestow prophethood upon whomever they wish and withhold it from whomever they wish. Or [it means]: they have the treasuries of His knowledge and wisdom, so that they could choose for it whomever wisdom requires to be chosen.

﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾ That is: the dominant ones over affairs, who manage them however they wish, so that they could manage the matter of lordship and build affairs upon their own will and volition. The reading "al-muṣayṭirūn" with the ṣād [instead of the sīn] was also recited, because of the ṭāʾ [in the root, i.e., the ṣād is used to assimilate to the ṭāʾ].

Verse 39: ﴿Has He daughters while you have sons?﴾ This is a rebuke to them and a disparagement of their intellects, and an announcement that one who holds such an opinion can hardly be counted among the sensible, let alone ascend to the world of the malakut (the realm of divine sovereignty) and gain insight into the unseen secrets. The shift to the direct address (khitab) serves to intensify the denial and reproach implicit in the disjunctive "am" (أمِ المُنْقَطِعَة, "am" used in the sense of "bal" plus interrogation).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 40:

﴿Or do you ask them for a payment?﴾ This is a return to addressing him (peace and blessings be upon him) and a turning away from them; that is, "Rather, do you ask them for a wage for conveying the message?"

﴿So they﴾ on account of that.

﴿are burdened with debt﴾ from undertaking a crushing penalty (gharam).

﴿burdened﴾ carrying a heavy load, and therefore they do not follow you.

(p-152) ﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they write it down?﴾ That is: the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), in which the unseen matters are recorded.

﴿So they write [what is in it]﴾, so that they might speak about that by way of negation or affirmation.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 42:

﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ It is their plot against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of the Quraysh).

﴿Then those who disbelieved﴾ are the ones mentioned. The placing of the relative pronoun (al-mawsul) in the position of their pronoun is for the purpose of recording against them what is in the scope of the relative clause (al-silah) of disbelief, and for giving the ruling a reason (ta'lil al-hukm) by it; or [it refers to] all the disbelievers, and they are included among them by primary inclusion (dukhul awwali).

﴿They are the ones who will be ensnared﴾: that is, they are the ones upon whom their plot will recoil, or upon whom its consequence will return, not those whom they intended to plot against. This is what befell them on the day of Badr. Or [it means] they are the ones who are defeated in the plot, from kayadtuhu (I outmaneuvered him), so kidtuhu (I outmaneuvered him in turn).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 43:

﴿Am lahum ilahun ghayru Allah?﴾ (Or do they have a god other than God?) That is, one who helps them and guards them from His punishment.

﴿Subhana Allah ʿamma yushrikun﴾ (Glory be to God above what they associate with Him). That is: above their associating (others with Him), or above the partnership of what they associate with Him.

The Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 44:

﴿And if they should see a fragment (kisf)﴾ a piece.

﴿falling from the sky﴾ for their punishment.

﴿they would say﴾ out of the excess of their transgression and obstinacy.

﴿A heaped-up cloud﴾ That is: they are so deep in transgression that if We were to drop it upon them, as they had demanded, or cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed, they would say: "This is a cloud piled up, one part upon another, that will rain upon us." They would not believe that it was a fragment falling as punishment.

So leave them until they meet ﴿that day of theirs in which they will be struck senseless﴾. It is also read as "حَتّى يَلْقَوْا" (until they encounter).

﴿يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي فِيهِ يُصْعَقُونَ﴾ is in the passive form (ʿalā al-binā' li-l-maf'ūl), from ṣaʿaqathu al-ṣāʿiqah (the thunderbolt struck him senseless) or from aṣʿaqathu (it struck him senseless). It is also read as "يَصْعَقُونَ" with a fatha on the yāʾ and the ʿayn, and then it means the day on which the stroke (al-ṣaʿqah) befalls them through killing, namely the day of Badr, not the first blast (al-nafkhah al-ūlā) as some have said; for no one is struck senseless by that blast except one who is alive at that time. And because the words of Allah, exalted is He:

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 46:

﴿The day when their scheming will avail them nothing at all﴾ i.e., nothing at all of availing. "The day" (yawma-hum) is in apposition (badal) to "their day." It is not hidden that the explicit statement of the futility of their scheming calls for the supposition that they employed it, hoping to benefit from it; and this is none other than the scheming they devised against his (ﷺ) affair, of which their opposition on the day of Badr (Badr) forms part. As for the first blast of the Trumpet (al-nafkhah al-ula), it is not among the matters in which scheming and stratagems can avert anything. It has also been said: it is the day of their death, and there is in this what there is, along with what the idiom of the annexation (al-idafah), which indicates that it is specific to them, rejects.

﴿Nor will they be helped﴾ from any other party in warding off the punishment from them.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 47:

﴿And indeed, for those who did wrong﴾ — i.e., for them. The placing of the relative pronoun (alladhina) in the position of the pronoun (them) is for what was mentioned before, i.e., "indeed, for these wrongdoers".

﴿a punishment﴾ — another.

﴿short of that﴾ — short of what they encountered of killing, i.e., before it, which is the famine that afflicted them for seven years, or after it, as in the verse of the poet:

"It shows you the mote from beyond it... and it is beyond it" (tureeka al-qadha min duniha... wa huwa duniha)

and it is the punishment of the grave and what follows it of the various kinds of punishment of the Hereafter. It was also recited as "short of that, near" (duna dhalika qariban).

﴿But most of them do not know﴾ — that the matter is as mentioned. In this there is an indication that among them are those who know that, but persist in disbelief out of obstinacy, or who know nothing at all.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 48:

﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾: by deferring them until their promised Day, and by leaving you among them while you endure sorrows and bear anxieties.

﴿For indeed you are under Our eyes﴾: that is, under Our protection and safeguarding, such that We watch over you and guard you. The plural "eyes" (a'yun) is used to correspond to the plural pronoun ("Our"), and to signal the utmost care in protection.

﴿And glorify﴾: that is, declare Him far exalted above whatever is not befitting to Him, while remaining in a state of [praising Him].

﴿with the praise of your Lord﴾: for His blessings, which are beyond enumeration (the preposition "with" here being for the sense of accompaniment).

﴿when you arise﴾: from wherever you stand. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ata' said: that is, say when you rise from your sitting: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You." Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: its meaning is: pray to Allah when you rise from your sleep. Al-Dahhak and al-Rabi' said: when you rise for the prayer, say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; blessed is Your name and exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You."

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 52, verse 49:

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾, is a singling out of part of the night for glorification, because worship during it is harder on the soul and further from showing off (riya'), as is hinted at by placing it before the verb.

﴿And at the setting of the stars﴾, i.e., at the time of their setting (idbar, "the back-end" or "the aftermath") at the end of the night, i.e., their disappearance by the light of dawn. It was also said: the glorification "during the night" refers to the two evening prayers (al-'isha'ayn), and "the setting of the stars" refers to the dawn prayer (salat al-fajr). It is also read "wa-adbara al-nujum" with a fatha, meaning: in its aftermath, when the stars have set or become hidden.

From the Prophet (ﷺ), upon him be blessings and peace: "Whoever recites Surat al-Tur, it is a right upon Allah, exalted is He, that He grant him security from His punishment and that He bless him with comfort in His Paradise."
